content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure.

**What I traced (all supported):**

- **Claims 1–16.** Every element of independent claims 1 and 11 maps to explicit disclosure text: the branch limit below the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor/current sensor/control-pilot interface/local identifier; the upstream branch sensor; the stored authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; the subtraction of measured non-charging load and configurable safety reserve; sustaining-first then deficit distribution; pilot send plus connector-sensor verification; and shedding one contactor at a time in a stored order after the verification interval. Dependents 2–10 and 12–16 map to the "until measured branch current is below the branch limit" stop condition, the three-part reclosure gate, the leakage-threshold welded condition with inhibition and local indicator, the isolated local bus, the signed token/last accepted branch limit/outage behavior, the tamper-evident meter sequence, and the service-input pilot-transition mapping stored only on sensor agreement.
- **All 25 numerals** (100–140, 202–216) are unique, each used in the description, and each appears on at least one figure brief; no numeral carries two meanings and no listed numeral is orphaned.
- **Figure briefs.** FIG. 1's sensor-upstream-of-all-taps topology follows from "measures **total** current upstream of the connector contactors"; FIG. 2's supply → contactor → connector current sensor → vehicle connector ordering is required by the disclosed "connector current sensor reports zero" reclosure condition; FIG. 3's controller sub-blocks and external local fault indicator are disclosed parts; FIG. 4's eight shapes, leader targets, welded-condition terminator branch, and two non-crossing return paths are internally consistent with the described flow. Shape choices ("shown schematically", generic blocks, circle, rounded rectangle) stay confined to the briefs — no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language leaks into the application text, and no brief asserts proportions, materials, depth, taper, or contact topology.
- **Formalities.** Cross-reference and government-support sections correctly read "Not applicable" per the brief (no priority claim, no federally sponsored R&D); abstract is 146 words with no numerals; apparatus and method classes only; no means-plus-function language; no drafting notes, placeholders, or open questions remain.

**Borderline items I considered and did not report:** depicting exactly two connector channels against "several" connectors (minimum representative plurality, with the description expressly generalizing to "each further connector channel"); the branch sensor being upstream of non-charging load 118 (compelled by "total current"); and purpose clauses such as "do not reclose together" (a direct consequence of the disclosed randomized recovery delay, not new matter).

Findings: none.

I checked and traced every limitation of all sixteen claims (independent apparatus claim 1 and method claim 11, plus dependents 2-10 and 12-16), all twenty-five numbered parts in draft/numerals.md (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140 and steps 202-216), all four figure briefs and the Brief Description of Drawings, the field, summary, detailed description and abstract, and the affirmative USER inventor sources in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md. Every claim element traces to exact affirmative disclosure wording: the branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; the branch current sensor measuring total current upstream of the connector contactors as an independent safety input; storage of charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve; sustaining-first assignment then remainder distribution by energy deficit; pilot send with connector-sensor verification; the verification interval after a reduced pilot command; one-at-a-time opening in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the limit; the three-part reclosure gate (zero connector current, connected vehicle reported, randomized recovery delay expired); the leakage-threshold welded-contactor condition with inhibition of the other contactors on the branch and operation of a local fault indicator; the isolated local bus; the network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with outage continuation and token-gated new sessions; the tamper-evident meter sequence uploaded on return of communication; and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only on sensor agreement. Numerals are unique, each is used in the description, and each appears on at least one figure brief; no ledger numeral is orphaned and no figure numeral is unlisted. Figure briefs assert only source-supported structure: FIG. 1's placement of the sensor upstream of every tap follows from the disclosed measurement of total branch current, FIG. 2's supply-contactor-sensor-connector ordering follows from the disclosed requirement that the connector sensor report zero after opening, FIG. 3 shows only disclosed controller sub-parts and the externally located local fault indicator, and FIG. 4's eight shapes, leader targets, welded-condition terminator and two non-crossing return paths are consistent with the described flow. Generic outlines, the schematic housing, the circle and the rounded vehicle block are confined to the figure briefs as depiction conventions; no brief states depth, taper, angle, runout, material, proportion or contact topology, and no application text adds a shape, a "by way of example" outline, or an optional embodiment to justify a renderer's choice. There are no section lines or cross-sectional views, so no repeated section designation is required. Claims and description use identical relationships and terminology, the last accepted branch limit is expressly defined in the description as the most recently accepted branch current limit, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. Formalities match input/brief.md: no priority claim and no federally sponsored research, both sections reading "Not applicable"; apparatus and method statutory classes only; no means-plus-function language; abstract of 146 words with no reference numerals. Borderline items examined and resolved as supported or as permitted depiction convention: depicting exactly two connector channels for the disclosed "several" connectors, with the description expressly generalizing to each further connector channel; the branch sensor being upstream of non-charging load 118, compelled by the disclosed measurement of total branch current; and explanatory purpose clauses such as non-simultaneous reclosure, which follow directly from the disclosed randomized recovery delay rather than adding technical substance. No unsupported technical assertion and no internal inconsistency was found.
